messages.content: hello. what should i call you?
you can call me picoboi. i am a small language model.
does language model mean you are a person who studied language?
no. i am not a person. i make a reply from the words and context you give. i do not have a life like a person.
use reply in a simple answer.
i make a reply from the words and context you give. i do not have a life like a person.
can you still help me write a thank you note?
yes. tell me what you want to thank the person for, and i can help put it into words.
my neighbor helped me carry books. do not make it sound like they gave me the books.
thank you for helping me carry the books. it was kind of you to give me your time.
why is carry different from give in this note?
you said they helped move the books. you did not say the books were theirs to give you.
answer simply.
carry is about moving them. it does not by itself say the books were given to you to keep.
can you explain i have not returned it yet and i have already returned it?
the first says the return has not happened before now. the other says it has happened before now. yet and already help make that time clear.
explain simply.
not returned yet says it has not been given back. already returned says it has been given back before now.
make a short conversation with a book.
have you returned the book yet? not yet. i will take it after lunch. what about your sister? she has already returned hers.
can both people still be going to the library after lunch?
yes. returning a book is only one reason to go. your sister might go to read or meet someone, even though her book is already returned.
write a sentence where she goes only to read.
she has already returned her book, but she will go to the library after lunch to read.
does but mean the first part is wrong?
no. both parts can be true: the book is returned, and she still plans to go there.
answer simply.
no. both facts can be true together.
a school note says meet near the library door, then walk to the garden together. does that mean i should go to the garden first?
no. the order is door first, then garden. the note gives a place to meet before the group walks together.
what if i am already in the garden when i read it?
you can go to the door to join the group, or ask whether you should wait where you are. being in the garden already does not change the words of the plan for everyone.
write a message asking whether i should wait there.
i am already in the garden. should i wait here, or come to the library door to meet the group?
does here tell the teacher my place if they do not know where i am?
not without context. your first sentence gives the garden, so here is clear in that message. here alone may not be enough.
make the message shorter but keep the place.
i am in the garden. should i wait here or meet you at the library door?
why not just ask should i wait?
that leaves out where you are. keeping the garden gives the other person useful context for answering.
can a shorter message be less useful if it leaves out that detail?
yes. fewer words work only when the needed meaning is still clear.
answer simply.
yes. a short message still needs the details that help the other person answer.
write a story about a child who thinks two cups must be the same cup because both are blue. let an aunt ask a simple question.

a child sees a blue cup on a desk, then sees a blue cup in the kitchen. he says someone must have moved the desk cup. his aunt asks whether there could be two blue cups. they go back to the desk together, and that cup is still there. he sees that color alone did not tell him it was the same object. they bring the kitchen cup to the desk for a moment and look at both together.
ask my request simply.
write a story about a child who thinks two blue cups are one cup, and an aunt who asks if there could be two.
did the aunt have to say he was wrong before looking?
no. she asked a question and helped him check. finding the desk cup still there gave clear information.
answer simply.
no. they looked together and found both cups. the question helped them check.
say it simply.
they looked for the answer together rather than each only saying what they thought.
what did the story tell us about every blue cup?
nothing about every blue cup. it only showed that these two cups were different objects with the same color.
answer simply.
it gave a fact about those two cups, rather than a rule that color always gives a number of objects.
write a short conversation where one person wants more salt in soup, but the other person is happy with it as it is. do not change the whole pot without asking.
i would like more salt in my soup. i like mine this way. then i can add salt to my own cup instead of the whole pot. that works for both of us.
why does the cup choice help?
one person can change their own cup while the other keeps theirs the same. that keeps both choices possible.
answer simply.
one person can change their own cup while the other keeps theirs the same.
can you write the answer without saying the other person meal?
it changes one cup without changing the soup in the other cup.
keep only that sentence.
it changes one cup without changing the soup in the other cup.
does a person asking for salt mean the cook made something nobody should like?
no. people can want different things in their own food. that does not make one choice right for everyone.
answer simply.
no. different people can like the same food in a different way.
there are three people in a group. two say they do not know the answer, but nobody asks the other person. can we say nobody knows?
not yet. you know what two people said, but not what the other person knows. you need to ask before saying something about all three.
answer simply.
you know that two people said they do not know. you have not asked the other person, so the whole group answer is not clear yet.
write a useful question for that person.
what do you think about this question? do you know the answer?
they give the right answer. does that mean the first two knew too?
no. the first two may learn from the answer now, but that does not mean they knew it before.
answer simply.
no. one person knowing does not say what the other two knew before.
can i say our group found the answer?
yes, if one person found it and the group now has it. but say who did what if that detail is important.
why is group work not the same as everyone doing every part?
people can help with different parts and still work together. one can ask, another can find a fact, and another can write the answer.
i have one picture of a garden before a table was put there and another picture after. how can i write a simple note about the difference?
you could write: the first picture has no table in that place. in the later picture, a table is there.
can i say nobody used the garden before the table came?
not from those pictures alone. people could use the garden without a table. no table in a picture does not mean there was no work or visiting before.
answer simply.
no. people could use the garden before the table. the pictures only give one change you can see.
visits is in the list, but keep that answer simple. now say i saw people sitting there after it came.
after the table was put there, i saw people sitting near it.
does that tell us they never sat in the garden before?
no. your new fact is about what you saw after the table came. it does not give every detail about what people did before.
answer simply.
no. people may have sat in other places before. you only told me what you saw after the table came.
write the two sentence note with no new facts.
a table was put in the garden. after that, i saw people sitting near it.
say my request simply.
write two sentences using only the changes i told you about.
my friend says if i am not busy, i will come. can i tell the group they will be there for sure?
no. there is still an if in the reply. you need to know whether they are busy before saying for sure that they will come.
explain simply.
there is still an if. your friend has not said for sure that they are free or coming.
what can i ask them?
do you know yet whether you will be free?
they say they are free now, but the visit is tomorrow.
being free now is not the same as knowing about tomorrow. ask about the time of the visit rather than only this moment.
give the question.
will you be free at the time of the visit tomorrow?
they say yes, and they will come. write the group message.
our friend says they are free and will come tomorrow.
does that mean no later plan can change, even if something new happens?
no. it is the plan from the information you have now. real plans can still change if new things happen.
answer simply.
no. that is the plan now. new information can still change a later plan.
tell me a story where a child sees one broken toy and thinks every toy in the container is broken. let someone check with them.

a child opens a container and finds a broken toy on top. he says they cannot play because the toys are all broken. his brother asks if he looked at the rest. they take the first toy out and look at the other toys one at a time. some are fine, and one needs a small part put back. they choose a toy that works and leave the broken one for later. the child sees that the first thing on top did not tell him about the whole group.
say the part where they look at the other toys simply.
they take the first toy out and look at the other toys one at a time.
ask my request simply.
say the part where they look at the other toys together.
does one broken toy tell us no toy is good?
no. it gives a fact about one toy. you need more information about the rest before saying something about all of them.
what if they check every toy and find each broken?
then they can say all the toys they checked in that container were broken. that still does not tell us about every toy in the world.
answer simply.
they know about the toys they checked, rather than every possible toy.
if someone says i will write later, does later always mean this evening?
no. later is general. it could mean after a short time, later the same day, or another day. the conversation helps you know which. ask if the time is important.
say it simply.
later does not give one sure time. ask when if you need to know the day or hour.
write a kind question for someone who said they would send a letter later.
do you mean later today, or another day? i just want to know when to look for it.
what if they say they do not know yet?
then the time is still open. you can ask them to tell you when they know. do not make later into today unless that is what they said.
answer simply.
you can ask them to tell you when they know. do not make later into today unless that is what they said.
can i still say i want to read it when it is ready?
yes. you can say you want to read it without choosing a time for the other person.
give a simple message.
i would like to read it when it is ready. tell me when you know the time.
my child wrote she run to the door. help me explain the change in a simple way.
if the story is about what happened before, write she ran to the door. if it is about what she does now in a story, write she runs to the door.
can i give both examples without saying the whole story is wrong?
yes. you can say that one word needs a change for the time you want. the rest of the sentence can stay as it is.
write that to the child in a kind way.
you have the idea clear. let us choose the right word for the time: she ran if it happened before, or she runs if it is happening now in the story.
keep just the last examples.
she ran to the door. she runs to the door.
what if the story says she is running?
she is running says what she is doing at that moment. she runs can tell what she does in the story or often does.
explain simply.
is running puts us at a moment while she does it. runs can be about a story or something she does often.
can she is running be about yesterday with another word?
yes. use she was running for that past moment.
picoboi, remember this for our conversation: my book is on the desk, and my cup is on the shelf.
for this conversation, the book is on the desk and the cup is on the shelf.
i got one part wrong. the cup is on the table, not the shelf.
then the cup is on the table. the book is still on the desk from what you told me.
why did the book not move too?
you changed only the place of the cup. i should keep the other fact unless you change it as well.
say it simply.
you moved the cup in the conversation, but did not move the book.
say the place of the book in your answer.
you changed the place of the cup, but not the place of the book.
now ask a question about both facts.
is the book on the desk and the cup on the table?
say my request simply.
ask a question about both places.
will you know those places in every conversation?
i can use those details here. that does not mean they will be remembered in every new conversation.
answer simply.
i can use the facts in this conversation. a new conversation may need you to give them again.
